issues.description: The problem statement and intended UML describe lectureName as a String attribute, but the solution implementation changes the field type to a LectureName class. This cross-artifact type difference (String vs. LectureName) is a structural mismatch that will confuse students about the expected type for the lectureName attribute and the corresponding constructor/getter/setter signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the lectureName type consistent across artifacts. Either revert the solution to use a String for lectureName (preferred to match the UML and problem statement), or update the problem statement and template to document and teach the LectureName wrapper type and adjust method signatures accordingly. Ensure constructor and getter/setter signatures match the chosen type.

issues.description: In the solution, getLectureName() is declared to return String but its implementation returns the LectureName object. This creates a method return type inconsistency within the solution and will cause compile errors or confusion when students inspect the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent with the field type. If lectureName remains a String, change the field to String and have getLectureName() return String. If using LectureName is intentional, change getLectureName() signature to return LectureName (and update the problem statement/template accordingly).

issues.description: In the solution, setLectureName(String) accepts a String parameter but assigns it to a field typed as LectureName, causing a parameter-to-field type mismatch in the setter implementation. This inconsistency will cause compile errors in the solution and confuses students about the expected setter signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the setter parameter type with the field type. If lectureName is intended to be a String, change the field to String. If lectureName should be a LectureName object, change setLectureName parameter to accept a LectureName (or provide an overload) and update the problem statement/template to reflect this design choice.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML describe the lectureName attribute as a String (lectureName) and expect a constructor and getters/setters around that String attribute. The solution implementation instead introduces a separate LectureName type/class and uses it as the type of the lectureName field and constructor parameter (while some methods in the solution still use String in signatures). This introduces a mismatched identifier/type for the same conceptual entity 'lecture name' across artifacts and will confuse students trying to map the exercise description to the provided implementation and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of the lecture name consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) revert the solution to use a plain String for the lectureName field, constructor parameter and getter/setter signatures (matching the problem statement and template), or (B) update the problem statement and template to explicitly introduce and document the LectureName class as the intended type (adjust UML, constructor signature and getter/setter types accordingly). Prefer option (A) for minimal cognitive load and to match the exercise description.
